summary: Not established. Apple's website terms bar automatic programs from accessing its sites, so the page was not captured, and nothing in this repository shows the iCloud sign-in markup or whether it sits in a frame on another origin. The profile stays manual.

sources.title: Apple Website Terms of Use, section Your Use of the Site
Hosted dashboard profiles: the iCloud entry and its limits

staysInteractive.note: Apple Account verification on a trusted device; named by the repository's profile text, never exercised.

lookedFor: Apple Website Terms of Use, read in full. They cover www.apple.com and all associated sites linked to it by Apple, and state: You may not use any deep-link, page-scrape, robot, spider or other automatic device, program, algorithm or methodology to access, acquire, copy or monitor any portion of the Site. www.icloud.com is an Apple site and was treated as covered, so https://www.icloud.com/ was not captured. iCloud's own service terms were not read.
robots.txt of www.icloud.com: it allows the root path. It was not the reason for skipping the capture.

docs/hosted-dashboard-profiles.md line 67 and the profile text: the iCloud website signs in with an Apple Account and device verification, and app-specific passwords are not website passwords. No markup is recorded.
This repository: no fixture, adapter, test or route catalog names an Apple sign-in control, a frame or an identity origin for iCloud.
The frame question. The plan records as recollection, not as a finding, that the sign-in fields sit in a frame served from another origin. Nothing read here confirms or refutes it.
Apple's help pages were not read: they belong to the sites the terms cover, and help pages show screenshots, not markup.
neededFromUser: The sign-in page saved from the user's own browser as "Webpage, Complete", read with --from-file. Its top document shows whether the fields are in the page or in a frame and names the frame's address. If they are in a frame, that frame's own document saved the same way is needed as well. Save any page signed out and with no password typed in; keep the "_files" folder beside the .html and both outside the repository: they can hold the account name.
notes: If the fields prove to be in a frame on another origin, the steps format cannot express the login: a step's frame is same-origin only, and releasing a credential into a cross-origin frame is question Q8, not approved. Until then no steps file is written under any evidence.
